candidates.name: Palma Cathedral
candidates.hours: April to November: Mon-Fri 10:00-17:15, Sat 10:00-14.15; December to March Mon-Fri 10:00-15:15, Sat 10:00-14:15
candidates.content: Huge ornate cathedral, impressive outside and within. It was started in 1229 but only completed in 1601, in mostly Gothic style; Gaudí had a go at improving it but quit in a strop. The Royal Chapel is the resting place of kings Ja

candidates.name: Royal Palace of La Almudaina
candidates.hours: April to September: Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00; October to March Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00
candidates.content: The fortress dates back to Roman times but what you see now is a rebuild from 1309. The ground floor is medieval while the upper floor, added in the 16th century, has the grand state rooms and suites. It was a seat of the kings of

candidates.name: Castell de Bellver
candidates.content: An unusual circular castle enclosing a courtyard, built in the 14th century over a Moorish fort. A circle is not the best design in the age of artillery, but there's an outer ravelin and it withstood two sieges. Within is a museum

candidates.name: Pilar and Joan Miro Foundation
candidates.content: Joan Miró lived mostly in Barcelona and Paris but had extended spells in Palma. His two former studios display 6000 works, and there's a sculpture garden.

candidates.name: Fundación Juan March Palma
candidates.content: Museum of modern art, a branch of the Madrid foundation of financier Juan March Ordinas (1880-1962). Big names on display here include Picasso, Miró and Dalí, and the building is a stately 17th century mansion.

candidates.name: Llotja de Palma
candidates.content: Medieval mercantile building with impressive architectural features, near the waterfront. It is occasionally used as event space but stands empty most of the time.

candidates.name: Palma Aquarium
candidates.content: Aquarium focused on Mediterranean and coastal ecosystems, with a huge shark tank and vast collection of live corals. Reservations advised.

candidates.name: Basílica de Sant Francesc
candidates.content: Church and cloister founded in 1281, in similar style to the cathedral but without the tourist hordes. The Franciscan nuns moved in with the Poor Clares in the 19th century.

candidates.name: Banys Àrabs
candidates.content: Sauna baths built in the tenth century, with under-floor heating; it's the only building in Palma dating to the Arab settlement. Only two or three small rooms are open, but there's a pleasant courtyard garden.

candidates.name: Museum of Mallorca
candidates.content: Small museum of city heritage, crowded with artworks.

candidates.name: Pueblo Español
candidates.content: "Village" containing replicas of notable Spanish buildings. In season there are artisan shops, restaurants and bars within, and it's an events venue, but it's a bit hollow at other times.

candidates.name: Museu Històric Militar de Sant Carles
candidates.content: Military museum in a 17th century Vauban-style bastion by the harbour.

candidates.name: Es Baluard Museu d'Art Contemporani
candidates.content: Three-storey collection of 19th-20th century works by artists from the Balearic islands.

candidates.name: Aqualand El Arenal
candidates.content: This water park has slides and pools for kids of all ages.

candidates.name: Abaco
candidates.content: Pricy and posy cocktail bar in a former coaching house, no food and reckon €20+ per cocktail. But you come for the over-the-top decor and atmosphere: Fridays at 23:30, the classical background music rises to a crescendo and fresh

candidates.name: La Cuadra del Maño
candidates.content: Popular barbecue restaurant with steak grilled over a wood fire. Great service and value for money.

candidates.name: Es Badulake
candidates.content: Sandwich shop, also with wraps and tacos, lots of vegan alternatives. Takeaway only, eat in the shade on the adjacent Passeig del Born.

candidates.name: Ca n'Ela Vegan Restaurant
candidates.content: All-vegan restaurant, some dishes are gluten-free. Menus change daily.

candidates.name: A Estribor
candidates.content: Small Chinese cafe bar, fast friendly service.

candidates.name: Casa Julio
candidates.content: Trad homemade food in a popular cafe, you may have to queue.

candidates.name: Es Raconet
candidates.content: Great home-cooked food for a bargain price.

candidates.name: Calixto
candidates.content: Paella is all they serve, and it's good.

candidates.name: Cappuccino Palau March
candidates.content: Good all-day place for breakfast and light bites.

candidates.name: Oh Mallork Bar de Tapas
candidates.content: Cozy friendly tapas restaurant.

candidates.name: Pesquero
candidates.content: Portside restaurant for seafood, paella, tapas and the like. Mixed reviews on whether it's worth what you pay.

candidates.name: A Ma Maison
candidates.content: French Tunisian homemade dishes, a one-man show. Vegan, GF and other diets no problem.

candidates.name: Boira Restaurante
candidates.content: Great value for their day-long Med cuisine.

december.text: Festa de l’Estendard is an end-of-year event in December, with a Mass at La Seu.
City centre has Arlequin, Es Petit Bar, Bar Savoy, Gibson Bar, Bar Nicholas, Can Frasquet and Manto Negro.
